written.q: What does your course say about swarm intelligence, and where does it sit among AI techniques?
written.a: Swarm intelligence (SI) is behaviour inspired by ants, birds and similar groups. It is one of the classical and complementary AI techniques, alongside genetic algorithms (inspired by evolution), fuzzy logic (degrees of truth) and rule-based systems, and beside machine learning. These methods can be hybridised (e.g. learning classifier systems combine GA and ML). Particle swarm and ant colony optimisation also appear on the GA slides' meta-heuristic map. Your folder contains nothing more on SI.

written.q: (Background) Compare swarm intelligence and genetic algorithms.
written.a: Both are nature-inspired, population-based meta-heuristics that need only objective values, not derivatives. A GA evolves chromosomes by selection, crossover, mutation and replacement; in swarm methods the agents (ants, particles) persist and are guided by their own experience and that of neighbours (pheromone trails, pbest and gbest).

written.q: (Background) Explain ant colony optimisation, including pheromone, positive feedback and evaporation.
written.a: Ants deposit pheromone as they walk and prefer stronger trails. A shorter path is completed faster, so it collects more pheromone (positive feedback) and more ants choose it; evaporation (τ ← (1 − ρ)τ + deposits) fades poor paths. Example: pheromone 4 vs 1 gives P(short) = 0.8; after 6 ants deposit 1 each on the short path and 2 deposit 0.5 on the long one with ρ = 0.5, the values are 8 and 1.5, so P(short) = 0.84.

written.q: (Background) Perform one PSO update for x = 4, v = 1, pbest = 3, gbest = 1, w = 0.5, c<sub>1</sub> = c<sub>2</sub> = 1.5, r<sub>1</sub> = 0.4, r<sub>2</sub> = 0.6 minimising f(x) = x².
written.a: vnew = 0.5×1 + 1.5×0.4×(3 − 4) + 1.5×0.6×(1 − 4) = 0.5 − 0.6 − 2.7 = −2.8. xnew = 4 − 2.8 = 1.2. f falls from 16 to 1.44, so the particle moved towards the swarm's best.
